decisive_items: heterozygous mutation (c.754G>A, p.A252T) in the HTRA1 gene
lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities (WMH)
lobe-dominant distribution of multiple cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) and relatively fewer CMBs in deep regions, mainly involving bilateral parieto-occipital lobes
response.rationale: The HTRA1 mutation is definitive for HTRA1-related hereditary cerebral small vessel disease, with supporting leukoencephalopathy and lacunar infarctions. CADASIL is caused by NOTCH3 mutations, and CAA/HCHWA are amyloid-related, neither matching the genetic result.

rejected.why: CADASIL syndrome is caused by NOTCH3 mutations, not HTRA1; the HTRA1 mutation is decisive against this label.
Same as R4; CADASIL is not supported by the HTRA1 mutation.
Lobar-predominant microbleeds suggest CAA, but the HTRA1 mutation and white matter/lacunar changes favor HTRA1-related small vessel disease.
HCHWA is amyloid-related and lacks support from the HTRA1 mutation; the genetic finding is more specific.
